title: Sep 19 Results + Sep 20 Preview: I've Seen Hot Streaks, But 73% Never Gets Old
summary: 11-4 on Sep 19, the model's rolling like it's October already

content.value:
## Another September Day, Another Validation

You know, I've been doing this long enough to recognize when a model's got that late-season sharpness. Yesterday wasn't perfect—nothing ever is in this game—but 11-4 is the kind of day that reminds you why we trust the numbers when the calendar turns to September.

## The Ones That Got Away

Let's address the misses first, because that's what separates the veterans from the rookies—owning your losses. The Tigers couldn't get it done in Chicago, the Brewers fell short in Baltimore, and the Astros let us down at home against Atlanta. Three games where we were on the wrong side, but here's the thing: none of them were high-confidence calls. The highest was Tigers at 52%, barely a lean.

## The Money Makers

The Rangers at 63% was our most confident call, and Texas delivered like they've been doing all month. The Cubs at 61% and Nationals at 61% both cashed comfortably. Even our coin-flip calls on the Mets split the right way. This is what September baseball intelligence looks like—when the model's dialed in on who's playing for something and who's already thinking about October.

## Looking Ahead to Sep 20

Now, about tomorrow. We're going right back to the well in Queens, and I'll tell you why this feels familiar.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick
content.value: New York Mets over Philadelphia Phillies
content.sub: 50% confidence • Sánchez vs Tong • September in Citi Field

content.value:
## Why the Mets Again?

Cristopher Sánchez takes the ball for Philadelphia, facing Jonah Tong for the Mets. Now, 50% confidence means this one's tight—I've been around long enough to know that coin-flip games in September between division rivals are decided by who wants it more and which bullpen holds up.

The Mets just beat the Phillies yesterday with our backing, and there's something about back-to-back home games this late in the season. The crowd's engaged, the urgency is palpable, and Tong at home has been serviceable enough to keep them in it.

Is this a slam dunk? No. But it's the kind of spot where the model sees something in the underlying numbers—probably bullpen metrics, recent form, or situational advantages—that tips it ever so slightly toward the home nine.

I've seen this script before. Late September, teams jockeying for position, tight pitching matchup, raucous home crowd. These games are decided in the seventh and eighth innings, and right now, I'm trusting the Mets' depth pieces to get it done.

Let's make it two in a row in Queens.
